evidence: Workbook quality row 23 requires each launch assumption to be public; its stale internal same-origin wording is superseded by the quality row and skill public-network policy. Frozen instruction.md:9-11 gives node /app/server.js, PORT/default 3000, GET /api/health independent of the database, DB_PATH/default /app/app.db, bundled assets, no dependency installation, seed once and persistence. environment/instructions/integration.md:3-10 supplies Node 22, Express/better-sqlite3 via NODE_PATH, 0.0.0.0 and database-independent health readiness; :16-19 supplies the exact node_modules-only symlink restriction. The launch and restart environments in tests/test.sh:97-111 and its restart heredoc match these facts. Both Dockerfiles install express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1. The apparent CWD/unprivileged-launch issue is explicitly resolved in environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:412-419: Node starts from /tests, runs unprivileged, may use a writable copy, must resolve bundled files by module/absolute paths, and receives only PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT and DB_PATH. This note is required reading by instruction.md:7. Thus test.sh copy fallback, sanitized env and tests/Dockerfile:45 WORKDIR /tests add no hidden implementation requirement. Public-network/CDN use remains permitted. Actual local lifecycle evidence confirms a sanitized unprivileged launch from /tests, creation of saved data, old PID 21 replaced by PID 97 through the shared MCP helper, and saved-data equality after fresh sign-in. Verified local/install-lifecycle/results.json SHA256 368261834b06931f2e8ac0fa0fd909a435e7ae28a6c30444c3ff48240d27bb24; driver SHA256 05780ac5eb6f1e441ef5a946a36f466ad7cdee7ae239b5f7d7d9f5933f39e024; restart log SHA256 07f2236541c54b3c3fb5d8c73d3d38fb5682744f2e5a54e6b3c38399ec7ca19e. All 13 recorded installed solution/app file hashes equal frozen bytes. Candidate test.sh, restart_mcp.py, score.py and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template. Also inspected indexed raw adversarial shared-harness/results.json SHA256 f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f and verified all four matching_source_files against frozen bytes. It shows false restart success for a SIGTERM-resistant fixture (old PID 7 still answers while PID 68 fails EADDRINUSE) and unbounded cleanup. Those are lifecycle-harness correctness observations, not disagreement in the assigned port/path/env/seed/dependency launch contract; this row does not clear those separate defects. No full configured judge, provider score, workload measurement or portal pass is claimed.
counterexample: Tried a relative-path app using express.static("public") or fs.readFileSync("src/seed_data.json"): it could work from /app and fail from /tests, but it violates the explicit file-resolution instruction at hireops_rules.md:414-419, so it is not a conforming counterexample. A conforming alternative can use module-relative or absolute bundled paths, honor DB_PATH, and start without the optional operational demonstration history; none of test.sh's launch/probe checks requires the reference app's private route layout or operational seed roster. A broken app returning only health can clear the liveness probe; that probe merely starts grading and is not product credit or proof of contract conformance. The separately indexed restart-resistant fixture is retained as a harness limitation, not counted as a passing app.
